title: With a Nushell filter on, a new folder's items or a search's results are first shown through the filter's answer for the last rows, usually as an empty list
problem: Found from two sides by reviewers, by reading, and read again by the orchestrator; nobody has seen it in the window yet. `apply_filter_to` (src/finder/filter.rs) starts a new `nu` run when the rows change (`filter_source != paths`), and goes on applying `self.filter_keep`, the set of paths the last run kept, until the new run answers: `if let Some(keep) = &self.filter_keep { rows.retain(|r| keep.contains(&r.entry.path)); }`. Only `set_filter` (a changed filter text) resets `filter_keep`. So when the rows are those of another place, the new rows are held against what the filter kept of the old place's rows, which is usually none of them: the list is empty for as long as `nu` takes to start and answer, then fills. From the reviewer of 'smart-folder-save-and-leaks' (done record, third item under 'Found, not fixed'): with a filter on, a search's first results can show cut down by a keep-set that wasn't made for them; for a Smart Folder the folder's run is the one `set_filter` starts just before the words are set. From the reviewer of 'results-scroll-reset' (done record): with a Nushell filter on, a search that ends shows the folder's items through the search's filter result until the filter has run again. By the same reading, every step from one folder to another with a filter on does it. What is not known: what the window shows in that time (an empty list, or also an empty-state message such as 'No Items'), and for how long on a real machine. The doc comment on `apply_filter_to` says 'Rows stay as they are until the first run finishes', which is true only of the first run after the filter text changes.
proposal: Reproduce first. The test executor runs a `nu` to its end in one step, so a test has to hold the run back: `AppState.nu` is the path of the program that is run (see how tests set it, and `nushell::filter_paths` in src/nushell.rs for what the program is given and must print), so a stand-in script that waits for a file to appear before answering would do, or a seam that lets a test hold `filter_task`'s answer; find the smallest honest way. Show, with a filter on: (a) folder A to folder B, (b) a folder to a search, (c) a search ending back to its folder, and what the list holds between the rows changing and the run's answer. Then decide what the list shows while a run for new rows is out, and say why. The cases differ: when the rows are the same place's, read again (a quiet reload after a file was added, the index finishing, a sort), the last keep-set is nearly right and keeping it avoids a flash of unfiltered items, which is surely why it is kept; when the rows are another place's or another search's, the last keep-set means nothing. So the keep-set should be dropped, or not applied, when the rows it was made for and the new rows are not the same place's and search's (the place, the words, the scope: find what identifies 'the same list' in the code; `filter_source` holds only paths). What to show instead while waiting: the first run after a filter text change shows the rows unfiltered until it answers, by design; doing the same here is consistent but flashes unfiltered items on every step; showing no rows with the filter bar's busy state (`is_filtering()`) and no empty-state message is the other choice. Look at both in pictures or frames and pick the one that a user stepping through folders with a filter on would rather see; the empty-state message ('No Items', 'This folder is empty') must not show while a run is out, whichever you pick. Selection: a `select` handed to a navigation (Back selects the folder you came from) is applied when the listing arrives; make sure it still lands when the filtered rows arrive later.
original_test_plan: Tests that fail today, with the run held back: with a filter on, after going from one folder to another the list never holds the new folder's items cut by the old folder's keep-set (it holds what your design says: all of them, or none with the busy state), and no empty-state message is shown while the run is out; the same from a folder to a search and from a search back; a quiet reload of the same folder (a file added) keeps the filtered list steady, with no flash of unfiltered items; when the run answers, the list is the filtered one and a selection asked for by the navigation is on its item. These need a real or stand-in `nu`: follow tests/controls.rs nushell_filter_and_smart_folders for how tests that need `nu` are written and skipped where it is missing (it is installed here at /usr/local/bin/nu).
original_risks: The filter runs on every change of rows, so flicker is the risk on both sides: unfiltered items flashing on each step, or the list blanking on each quiet reload. A slow filter (a pipeline that takes seconds) makes whatever is shown meanwhile stay for seconds: it must be honest (not look like an empty folder) and must not let the user act on items the filter will remove if that matters to a command. `set_filter` turns `run_search` on or off when the filter goes on or off during a search ('Turning it on or off changes how many results a search fetches'); a Smart Folder's `enter_smart_folder` and `leave_smart_folder` put filters in and take them out through `replace_filter`: read 'smart-folder-save-and-leaks' before touching the order of things there. 'live-search-results' (in flight in lane d) re-runs searches quietly; its rows are the same search's, so the keep-set should stay applied across them.

verifier.claim_check: Not checked by a second reviewer and never seen in the window: two reviewers traced it by reading on different commits, and the orchestrator read `apply_filter_to`, `start_filter` and `set_filter` on the trunk (60df179) and they are as described. Reproduce before changing anything. If the window turns out to show nothing wrong (for instance because something else already hides the rows while `filtering` is set), write the closed record with the evidence and return skipped.
verifier.implementation_notes: See the proposal: a starting point, not a checked plan.

orchestrator_notes: Read the done records of 'smart-folder-save-and-leaks', 'results-scroll-reset' and 'search-skeleton-flash' first (all on the trunk): they describe the order in which a search's rows, the filter and the placeholders are set up, and each has tests around `apply_filter_to`'s early return for a search that hasn't answered. From the reviewer of 'empty-state-messages' (f60d2e4, on the trunk; read its done record's note for this brief, which also shows how its test holds a filter run back without a stand-in script: `navigate` inside `ui.window`, then `ui.cx.executor().tick()` until `is_filtering()`). That change made one thing worse that is yours to calm: the empty-state message no longer shows while a run is out over items (render_content's message branch has `&& !(self.filtering && self.unfiltered_len > 0)`), so when 'No Items Pass the Filter' is up and the list under it changes (typing on in a search, a folder that gains an item, a quiet rerun from 'live-search-results', another sort) the area goes message, placeholders, message for the length of each `nu` run. When the rows are the same place's and search's, keep it steady, for instance by leaving the message up with its old count until the run answers. Do not widen that guard to plain `!is_filtering()`: an empty folder would flash placeholders.
